shifts.summary: Overall the shift was rated Moderate by most sources. Candidates reported attempting between 17 and 89 questions well. Reasoning and English were generally found easy, while Quant varied from easy to hard. General Awareness difficulty ranged from Easy to Moderate, with some reports calling it Difficult.

sections.name: General Intelligence & Reasoning
sections.notes: Reasoning described as easy or simple, some time‑consuming similar options, statement‑based and blood‑relation items common.

sections.name: General Awareness
sections.notes: GS described as moderate overall, some found it difficult or out of syllabus; topics covered history, art, economics, current affairs, polity, geography and specific indexes.

sections.name: Quantitative Aptitude
sections.notes: Quant ranged from easy‑to‑moderate to hard; many arithmetic and mensuration items, some advanced topics like statistics and probability, considered the toughest part by several candidates.

sections.name: English Comprehension
sections.notes: English reported as easy overall; cloze tests were straightforward, passages long and time‑tight for some, grammar and vocabulary items varied in difficulty.

intro: The SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam held on 9 October 2026 was analyzed across three shifts. Reported figures are unofficial and SSC normalises scores across shifts for final reporting. Shifts 1 and 2 were largely rated Moderate to Easy, while Shift 3 showed a Moderate to Difficult trend. The analysis for Shift 3 is still pending and will be added once the shift is fully reported.

faqs.q: What overall difficulty was reported for the SSC CGL 2026 Tier 1 exam on 9 October 2026?
faqs.a: Shifts 1 and 2 were mostly rated Easy to Moderate, whereas Shift 3 was reported as Moderate to Difficult. The combined view suggests a mixed difficulty level across the exam day.

faqs.q: How many questions were candidates able to attempt well on 9 October 2026?
faqs.a: Shift 1 saw good attempts ranging from 17 to 89 questions, Shift 2 reported an average of about 85 good attempts, and Shift 3 indicated 85‑90% of questions were attempted well. These numbers are unofficial and reflect candidate reports.

faqs.q: Which sections were considered easiest on 9 October 2026?
faqs.a: Reasoning and English were generally found easy in Shift 2, while General Awareness varied between Easy and Moderate across all shifts. Quantitative Aptitude showed mixed difficulty, being easy in Shift 2 but difficult in Shift 3.

faqs.q: Did time shortage affect any sections on 9 October 2026?
faqs.a: Yes, candidates in Shift 2 reported time shortage particularly impacting the Mathematics (Quantitative Aptitude) section and longer reading passages in English.

faqs.q: When will the complete analysis for Shift 3 of the 9 October 2026 exam be available?
faqs.a: The full analysis for Shift 3 will be added after the shift is fully reported and the data are consolidated.
